course.title: Node.js — From Beginner to Professional
course.description: A visual-first, project-based Node.js curriculum covering the runtime and core APIs through asynchronous execution, streams, HTTP, database-backed services, security, testing, observability, deployment, and professional system design.
course.version_scope: Teaching baseline: use a supported Node.js LTS release (Node.js 24 LTS as checked on 2026-10-13). The official releases page lists Node.js 26 as Current and Node.js 24/22 as LTS. Some advanced APIs, flags, permission behavior, embedded SQLite capabilities, module-loader hooks, and TypeScript integration are version-sensitive; verify the exact installed runtime. The Node.js 22 runtime available in the build-check environment is used only for syntax checks.
audience: learners preparing for professional Node.js engineering
prerequisites: JavaScript variables, functions, arrays, objects, promises, and async/await
Basic terminal use and file/folder concepts
HTTP fundamentals are introduced where needed
learning_outcomes: Explain the Node.js runtime, supported release lines, execution model, and core APIs.
Build CLIs, HTTP services, database-backed APIs, and real-time/background services.
Use asynchronous operations, streams, workers, tests, profiling, and diagnostics appropriately.
Design authentication, authorization, secure configuration, deployment, and operational controls.
Evaluate architecture trade-offs, specialized APIs, and version-sensitive integration choices.

source_correction_log.source_note: The PDF (Section A, page 2) lists Node.js 26 as Current and Node.js 24/22 as LTS as of 2026-10-10.
source_correction_log.verification: The official Node.js release page checked on 2026-10-13 lists Node.js 26.11.1 as Current and Node.js 24/22 as LTS.
source_correction_log.decision: Use a supported LTS runtime (Node.js 24) as the teaching baseline. Label APIs/flags that vary by runtime and link to current official documentation.

source_correction_log.source_note: Section A distinguishes JavaScript language fundamentals, the Node.js runtime, and third-party frameworks.
source_correction_log.verification: The Node.js introduction describes Node.js as a cross-platform runtime based on V8.
source_correction_log.decision: Retain this distinction and label Express/Fastify/Socket.IO-style topics as ecosystem integrations, not Node.js core APIs.

source_correction_log.source_note: Lessons 1–2 both introduce what Node.js is and how the runtime operates.
source_correction_log.verification: Both lesson titles and their separate subtopic sets are present in the source syllabus.
source_correction_log.decision: Keep both numbered lessons to preserve the 263-lesson source structure; separate the overview from runtime components in the lesson content.

source_correction_log.source_note: Module 27 and Section E include optional TypeScript/runtime integrations, embedded SQLite, WebAssembly, and other specialized APIs.
source_correction_log.verification: Node.js documentation labels version-sensitive features and publishes API stability information.
source_correction_log.decision: Keep the topics as optional/specialist coverage, with explicit version/toolchain checks; the CodeLeaf source project remains JavaScript/JSX and no TypeScript source files are added.

source_correction_log.source_note: Module 24 includes the Node.js permission model as a hardening topic.
source_correction_log.verification: Official docs state that the permission model is a seat-belt mechanism, not a security guarantee against malicious code.
source_correction_log.decision: Teach least privilege as defense in depth and require external OS/container isolation for untrusted code.

source_correction_log.source_note: Section C defines 24 practical exercises that include coding and systems investigations.
source_correction_log.verification: The current CodeLeaf playground is a browser preview and not an isolated Node.js runner; its backend supports only bounded graders.
source_correction_log.decision: Keep all 24 tasks separate with protected reference solutions and disclose that the current grader performs limited static-marker checks; advanced tasks require local execution/human review and should not be published as fully automated coding evaluations.

source_correction_log.source_note: Pages 51–53 show illustrative project screenshots; the PDF also has tables/roadmap/coverage visuals in Sections D–G.
source_correction_log.verification: All 57 PDF pages were rendered and inspected as a contact sheet, with project pages 51–52 reviewed at full size.
source_correction_log.decision: Do not copy project screenshots or third-party visuals. Create original accessible SVG roadmap, module overviews, and lesson concept maps.

source_correction_log.source_note: The source says to treat the 263 numbered lessons as the primary curriculum catalog.
source_correction_log.verification: All 263 sequential lesson titles and each indented subtopic list were extracted from Section B. Sections C–G were also represented in exercise/project files and course metadata.
source_correction_log.decision: Keep all titles/subtopics and add the source lesson number in each lesson file for traceability.

learning_roadmap.title: First programs
learning_roadmap.focus: Install a supported runtime, run scripts, inspect process state, and learn configuration.

learning_roadmap.title: Core development
learning_roadmap.focus: Modules, npm, system APIs, file operations, buffers, and events.

learning_roadmap.title: Asynchronous runtime
learning_roadmap.focus: Promises, scheduling, event-loop behavior, streams, and backpressure.

learning_roadmap.title: Build applications
learning_roadmap.focus: HTTP, external services, CLI tools, databases, and frameworks.

learning_roadmap.title: Secure and reliable systems
learning_roadmap.focus: Identity, authorization, real-time systems, jobs, tests, debugging, and diagnostics.

learning_roadmap.title: Production engineering
learning_roadmap.focus: Performance, hardening, reusable packages, deployment, architecture, and reliability.

learning_roadmap.title: Specialization and capstone
learning_roadmap.focus: Version-sensitive integrations, specialized APIs, and a production-ready commerce backend.

dependency_map.learn_first: JavaScript functions, objects, promises, and async/await

coverage_checklist: Runtime identity separated from language/framework topics
CommonJS and ESM with interoperability and resolution
Asynchronous execution, event loop, scheduling, streams and backpressure
Core APIs: filesystem, path, URL, buffers, process, events, networking, HTTP and utilities
Authentication, authorization, secure configuration and permission boundaries
Deployment, containers, CI/CD, graceful shutdown and runtime upgrades
Workers, native integrations, specialized APIs, architecture and reliability
